examples.question_text:
(a) Using $|ab|=|a||b|$, evaluate $|-6\times7|$.
(b) Check that $|a+b|\le|a|+|b|$ for $a=-9$ and $b=4$ by calculating both sides.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\begin{align*}|-6\times7|&=|-6|\times|7|\\&=6\times7\\&=42\end{align*}$

(b) $\begin{align*}\text{LHS}&=|-9+4|\\&=|-5|\\&=5\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\text{RHS}&=|-9|+|4|\\&=9+4\\&=13\end{align*}$

Since $5\le13$, the inequality holds for these values. The two sides are not equal.

examples.derivation: Independently calculated |-12|=12; |7-16|=|-9|=9; -6+|-14|=-6+14=8. These follow the source's magnitude and inside-first methods.
Independently calculated |8-(-5)|=13; |-20|/|3-8|=20/5=4. For part (c), the numerator is 7-12=-5 and the denominator is -6+1=-5, giving 1. All intermediate steps agree.
The product identity gives |-6×7|=6×7=42. For a=-9 and b=4, LHS=|-5|=5 and RHS=9+4=13; therefore 5≤13, with unequal sides. This checks the inequality for the specified values.
For t≥0, |t|=t; for t<0, |t|=-t. When t<5, t-5<0, so |t-5|=-(t-5)=-t+5. The conditions and results match the taught piecewise definition.
